heroHeadline: QUIET WEEK CONTINUES: LATVIA LAUNCHES 'NAMEJS '26' EXERCISE WITH US, CANADIAN, BALTIC TROOPS (SEP 2) AS PENTAGON POSTURE REVIEW GRINDS ON; NO NEW PUBLIC DEVELOPMENTS ON ARTICLE 5 CREDIBILITY SINCE AUG 31 BILD/TELEGRAPH REPORTING
heroSubtitle: As of September 4, 2026, the NATO-US tracker's dominant story remains the credibility of Article 5 deterrence amid the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review, with the only new verified development this week an operational one: Latvia launched its annual 'Namejs '26' national defense exercise on September 2, running through October 8, with roughly 12,000 troops including US, Canadian, Estonian and Lithuanian forces training under NATO's Multinational Division North. As with June's BALTOPS 26 drill, Namejs '26 underscores the recurring paradox of 2026 — NATO-US military integration continues at the operational level even as the political and budgetary foundations of the alliance remain unsettled. No new public developments have emerged on the Article 5 credibility question since German tabloid Bild and the UK's Telegraph reported August 31 on detailed scenarios for how Russia could test NATO short of a full invasion — from unrest in Estonia's Narva to a Suwałki Corridor push to Article 5-testing cyberattacks — which drew pushback from Baltic and Nordic leaders including Latvia's PM Kulbergs, Finland's President Stubb, Estonia's FM Tsahkna and Romania's Defence Minister Miruță, all of whom said they see no evidence of an imminent conventional attack even as Russian hybrid activity continues. NATO allies faced an August 29 deadline to submit written responses to the Pentagon's access-and-loyalty questionnaire (first disclosed by Bloomberg on August 14), but no consolidated public accounting of allied responses has emerged as of this update. Reuters continues to report the review will yield four sets of troop-level options for Hegseth by November 6, with the top US general in Europe due to brief Under Secretary Colby on force-level options by September 18.
